text: Resolve any user-supplied machine/equipment serial to the canonical identity BEFORE querying. Normalize the user token to uppercase alphanumeric, strip exactly one leading zero, and match the governed lookup key by equality (wo_header.source_serial_lookup_key / scheduler_appointment.appointment_serial_lookup_key, or the Serial-identity RAG dataset -> key_make_serial). NEVER use ILIKE or raw '=' against source_machine_serial_number (or raw serial columns) as the final identity test. Example: user serial ERM00299 -> canonical key_make_serial 'AA|0ERM00299'.
trigger: a specific serial number / machine / equipment identity question

text: Bound every SQL pass. The raw tables are huge (e.g. work_order_note_history ~72M rows, work_order_segment ~12.6M, parts ~90M), so every non-identity query MUST include at least one of: (a) an exact key equality (=) on serial / work-order / branch / appointment, (b) an inclusive date window on the relevant date dimension, or (c) an explicit LIMIT (default 100 rows) when materializing rows. Never scan a big table wholesale; prefer COUNT(DISTINCT ...) / aggregates over pulling rows.
trigger: any count / aggregate / join over large or unbounded tables

text: Never run LIKE / CONTAINS / ILIKE on work-order note text in SQL. Notes are indexed in the Note-text-search RAG dataset — if you catch yourself writing a note-text scan, stop and run a RAG search (search_dataset Note-text-search with the symptom/terms) instead.
trigger: symptoms / causes / repairs / issues / leaks / narrative in notes

text: For unbounded historical / trend / prior-work / cohort questions with no user-supplied period, filter the work-order open date from DATEADD(year, -1, CURRENT_DATE()) through CURRENT_DATE() inclusive (trailing 12 months) — and tell the user the window you applied. Exact work-order lookups are exempt.
trigger: unbounded trend / history / prior / cohort question without a period

text: Route by question type, not fixed ordering: narrative / repair / structural machine-history questions -> RAG (Note-text-search for narrative, Segment_summary for structural repair facts). Deterministic facts — exact counts, statuses, totals, date windows, cohort aggregates, scheduler/appointment state, technician travel — -> SQL through the governed surface, always bounded. Do not force a RAG round-trip for things SQL answers directly, and do not reach for SQL for narrative content RAG already indexes.
trigger: choosing RAG vs SQL for any question

text: Technician travel (e.g. 'who travelled the most') is the SUM of elapsed hours on travel-type charge codes 'TVL' and 'TVW' in the labour table, joined to scheduler technicians for names. Canonical: SELECT COALESCE(t.first_name||' '||t.last_name, wl.employee_number) AS technician, ROUND(SUM(wl.elapsed_hours),2) AS travel_hours, COUNT(*) AS travel_lines FROM work_order_labour wl LEFT JOIN scheduler_technicians t ON t.clock=wl.employee_number OR t.employee_id=wl.employee_number OR t.ukg_employee_number=wl.employee_number WHERE wl.charge_code IN ('TVL','TVW') AND wl.document_date >= (CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1' YEAR) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY travel_hours DESC LIMIT 20.
trigger: which technician travelled the most / travel hours / technician workload

text: Parse Serial-identity RAG hits by splitting on ' | ': the LAST part is the model, the MIDDLE part is the canonical key_make_serial (e.g. DU|SL40SE807E05607), and the leading space-separated tokens are the raw serial with/without a leading zero. Example: 'SL40SE807E05607 SL40SE807E05607 | DU|SL40SE807E05607 | SL40SE90D' -> machine DU|SL40SE807E05607, model SL40SE90D, serial SL40SE807E05607.
trigger: parsing a Serial-identity retrieval hit to resolve a machine

text: Note-text-search stores ONE doc per work-order note with content '<key_make_serial> | <model> | <note text>' so serial/model tokens embed verbatim. Never expect exact serial matches from vector search alone — for exact serial resolution use SQL (exact equality on the canonical key) and RAG for the repair narrative. Period filtering uses each doc's open_date/close_date metadata (no SQL needed).
trigger: understanding what Note-text-search holds / how to filter by period
